questions.prompt: What problem does NAT primarily solve?

options.text: Letting many private hosts share one public IPv4 address

questions.explanation: NAT works around IPv4 address scarcity by letting a whole private network share a single public IP address.

questions.prompt: In PAT (NAT overload), what does the router rewrite on outbound packets?

options.text: The source IP and source port

questions.explanation: PAT rewrites the source IP and source port; the unique translated port lets many hosts share one public IP and keeps replies sorted out.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of an outbound connection through NAT and its reply.

items.text: Internal host sends a packet with a private source IP
Router rewrites the source to its public IP and a unique port
Router records the mapping in its translation table
Reply arrives addressed to the public IP and port
Router translates it back to the private host

questions.explanation: NAT rewrites the private source to the public IP/port, records the mapping, and reverses it when the reply arrives so it reaches the right internal host.

questions.prompt: To let an external client reach an internal server through NAT, you configure a static rule called port ____.
questions.explanation: Port forwarding maps inbound traffic on a public IP/port to a specific internal host and port.

questions.prompt: Which statements about NAT are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Outbound connections create translation-table entries automatically
Unsolicited inbound packets are dropped unless a forward exists
IPv6 largely removes the need for NAT
NAT provides full network security by itself

questions.explanation: Outbound traffic builds mappings, inbound needs a forward, and IPv6 restores end-to-end addressing. NAT is not a security solution on its own.

questions.prompt: Match each NAT term to its description.

pairs.right: Maps inside connections to translated public ports
Static rule for inbound to reach an internal host
Rewriting ports so hosts share one public IP
Techniques (STUN/TURN) to connect peers through NAT

questions.explanation: The table tracks mappings, forwarding lets inbound in, PAT shares one IP via ports, and traversal helps peer-to-peer through NAT.
